title: Cross-environment rollforward/rollback handshake for canary regressions with data-residency constraints
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Playbook and orchestration notes for handling model canary regressions that require coordinated rollbacks or rollforwards across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments when customers have strict data-residency or network isolation constraints.
incident_summary: During a staged rollout of model v3.1 we observed a reproducible quality regression affecting structured output format for a subset of prompts. Canary telemetry exceeded the failure threshold (error_rate > 8% for 5m) in two Hosted regions and two Dedicated pools. One private customer reported a high-severity support ticket (incorrect PII redaction patterns) and required tenant-specific mitigation due to data-residency rules that prevent traffic diverting through alternate regions.
runbook_steps:
1) Triage: collect Grafana traces, request IDs, sample inputs. Post summary to #incidents and create a dedicated Slack huddle with SRE, Runtime, Support, PM, and Legal.
2) Scope: identify affected surfaces (text-generation structured output path, function-calling, embeddings) and enumerate affected tenants.
3) Canary containment: flip canary traffic to 0% for new rollouts; enable circuit breaker for the model variant (runtime route-level switch).
4) Decide rollback vs rollforward: evaluate footprint of fix and rollback blast radius. If fix < 24h and low-risk, prefer rollforward; otherwise perform rollback. Document trade-offs in Decision Log.
5) Tenant-specific mitigation: for Private/VPC customers with data-residency constraints, use model pinning at tenant routing layer rather than global rollback. Coordinate with on-prem engineering to apply the pinned config and restart inference agents if required.
6) KV cache and state considerations: when rolling back to previous model, clear/refresh per-tenant KV cache where structural format changed. For rollforward, publish a migration note and plan cache reset window.
7) Communication: send templated incident update to affected customers with ETA, mitigation path, and escalation contact.
8) Deploy: execute automated rollback playbooks for Hosted/Dedicated; for Private customers use remote config push and verify agent heartbeat.
9) Verify: run smoke tests, run canary traffic for 30 minutes with strict telemetry dashboards.
10) Postmortem and retrospective: include signal thresholds, test coverage gaps, and follow-ups for model & eval teams.
decision_log:
2026-03-02: Chose immediate canary cutoff in Hosted regions to stop user-facing failures (decision by Marco Li, Aisha Kapoor). Reason: high customer impact and reproducible failure pattern.
2026-03-03: For Dedicated pools with SLA commitments, we performed targeted rollback to v3.0 for two pools; trade-off: slight latency regression vs incorrect output risk.
2026-03-04: For one Private customer (EU-data region) we applied tenant-level pin to v3.0 instead of routing through another region because of data-residency legal constraints (decision documented by Legal and PM Sophie Martins).
2026-03-06: Decided to implement a short-term code patch (rollforward) for structured-output sanitization with validation harness to avoid repeated rollbacks; schedule patch release in runtime-2.4. Trade-off: patch required extra QA hours but avoided cross-tenant cache invalidation.
reviewer_feedback:
SRE review (Olivia Chen): added KV cache per-tenant clear step and emphasized monitoring of cold-cache latency.
PM review (Sophie Martins): requested customer-facing language to include mitigation steps for self-serve Dedicated tenants.
Design review (Evan Brooks): suggested adding a quick-check end-to-end test to the canary job to catch format regressions.
Security review (Rohit Verma): confirmed tenant pin approach satisfies data-residency constraints but requested an audit entry for the config change.
timeline_summary: 2026-03-01: Canary alerts in two Hosted regions; 2026-03-01 02:00: Immediate canary cutoff and incident huddle; 2026-03-03: Dedicated pool rollback applied to two pools; 2026-03-04: Tenant pin applied for affected Private customer; 2026-03-06: Rollforward patch acceptance tests green; 2026-03-09: Incident moving to monitoring with reduced customer escalations.
next_actions:
1) Automation: add a tenant-scoped pin API to Console for faster private-customer mitigation (owner: Backend).
2) Tests: add structured-output regression to the canary validation suite (owner: Applied ML).
3) Observability: create a per-tenant deviation SLO dashboard and alert (owner: Observability).
4) Follow-up EPIC: refine rollout policy to prefer rollforward when fix ETA < 12h (owner: Product).
5) Postmortem: schedule blameless review and publish to customers by 2026-03-16.
